Author: @blwarren
Content:
This is a fascinating and well-produced explanation of how the Vatican functions as a sovereign entity, but it misses an important part of the story — the why behind that sovereignty. The Vatican isn’t meant to be a “country” in the conventional sense. Its existence isn’t about borders, an economy, or a resident population; it’s about ensuring the Church’s independence from any government so it can serve a worldwide community of over a billion Catholics.

It’s also misleading to treat the Holy See’s diplomacy as if it were just another political player “backing winners.” The Holy See’s engagement on global issues — from peace negotiations to bioethics — is grounded in moral and theological principles, not popularity or strategy. When the Vatican mediates conflicts or speaks at the UN, it does so as the spiritual voice of a truly international Church, not as a European microstate.

In short, the Vatican’s uniqueness isn’t that it’s a tiny state with embassies; it’s that it’s the visible instrument of a faith that transcends nations, languages, and cultures. The sovereignty of the Holy See exists precisely because the Church must be free to speak to all nations — not as one among them, but as a universal moral witness above them.

Author: @georgeli3935
Content:
The official name has always been the Holy See. The term Vatican is a misnomer applied to the Holy See. The Vatican is its territory. For similar reasons Monaco and Monte Carlo is also often mixed up.

The Holy See has always been involved in European politics. When it lost its territory, this doesn't automatically mean they lose international recognition. Governments in exile are often considered a legitimate government, despite having zero territory. Whether or not a "state" has territory is almost irrelevant. You are a sovereign state when others recognise you as a sovereign state. For all purposes Taiwan is a state, but without recognition, it isn't. The Holy See is on the other spectrum. It is a state purely because other countries recognises it as one.

"the Vatican" is actually the name of the physical territory of the "Holy See" which is the proper term of the government of the Vatican city state. Nations do not have relations to the "Vatican" proper but the Holy See.
The "Government" of the Vatican and the Catholic Church, is the Roman Curia. The Roman Curia, is lead by the Secretary of State, effectively the Prime MInister of the Holy See, and often seen as the second in charge, of the Catholic Church.
Then there is the Camerlengo, who is the Chamberlain of the Papacy, and only temporarily occupies the powers of the Pope as steward of the Church in the situations of Sede Vacante when there is no pope and conclave has not elected a successor yet.
And the Pope is more properly a "Sovereign" rather than a King.
